A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HalluEditBench and provide readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices. Rendered inspection supports matching the experiments despite revised plots, appendix renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre/post-edit experiments in Table 1 and evaluates seven editing methods on three LLMs across five facets, including domain-level appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised benchmark scores in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The benchmark framework and descriptions of the seven editing methods remain substantively unchanged in Sections 2.1–2.3 and Appendix B. The revised question-generation prompt concerns evaluation-data construction; no editing algorithm, architecture, loss, or inference component is introduced or modified.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same nine domains, 26 topics, five evaluation facets, and preliminary WikiDatarecent, ZsRE, and WikiBio comparisons. Changing 'Wikipedia' to 'Wikidata' clarifies the source already identified through Wikidata Query Service in v1. Replacement appendix examples remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The benchmark retains FT-L, FT-M, MEMIT, ROME, LoRA, ICE, and GRACE, with the same comparator membership in corresponding figures. Table 1 retains its five post-edit comparators. Additional citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A revises the portability-generation prompt to supply the one-hop question and answer alongside subject/relation, explicitly nest preceding questions, and exclude preceding answers. This changes the reported evaluation-data construction instructions; the PDFs do not establish whether questions were regenerated or experiments rerun. Metrics, model checkpoints, hop ranges, and conversation-turn ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same domain analyses, one-to-six-hop portability tests, and ten-turn robustness tests remain in the main text and corresponding appendices. No additional ablation, sensitivity study, or analytical case study appears. Revised scores and illustrative QA examples do not establish a new analytical test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Generalization plots continue to depict pre-edit and post-edit scores, with no added statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerous domain-level scores change across the main and appendix figures. For example, Figure 6 reports ICE locality on Llama2-7B/places at roughly 48% in v1 versus 66% in v3; Figure 16(c) changes GRACE's turn-zero robustness from 0% to approximately 95%. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance gains. Table 1 remains unchanged. Appendix examples are also replaced, and Fiat's inconsistent efficacy answer is corrected to Giovanni Agnelli.

T1.justification: The knowledge-editing triplet definition and evaluation-score definitions are retained. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs, and v3 adds no substantive mathematical assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution—a verified hallucination benchmark evaluating five facets—remains unchanged. The introduction modestly qualifies the portability claim: methods other than ICE 'underperform' pre-edit models in v1 but 'could' underperform in v3. The revised conclusion largely restates criticisms already present in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes the categorical inference that LLMs cannot reason with edited knowledge regardless of editing method to saying they may not do so for most methods. Section 3.5 narrows the high-robustness examples to MEMIT and ROME, removing FT-M/FT-L from that characterization. New Appendix D discusses the work's implications for combating misinformation.

D1.justification: Section 2.1 adds the Wikidata query date, September 8, 2024, and states that each topic initially has at least 100 triplets. Appendix A provides the revised generation prompt but removes the previously specified count of eight GPUs. GPU type, decoding temperature, checkpoint links, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C substantially expand cited coverage, including MMKE-Bench, MC-MKE, The Mirage of Model Editing, newer lifelong editing methods, and editing-safety research. New Appendix D additionally positions the work within misinformation detection, intervention, attribution, and retrieval-augmented generation literature. These additions extend beyond publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: v3 makes distributed wording corrections and limited paragraph rewrites while retaining the main narrative and section sequence. It updates affiliations and headers, adds acknowledgments and an Impact Statement, and revises the appendix illustrations. These are limited structural and editorial changes.

P2.justification: The figure set and basic chart designs remain, with presentation refinements: generalization plots add endpoint markers, Figure 8 reverses the human/places panel order, and Figures 15 and 18 change from vertical arrangements to horizontal rows sharing pages with preceding figures. Plot sizing, spacing, and captions also receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects demonstrable inconsistencies, including Fiat's answer and GRACE's zero-turn robustness in Figure 16(c), improves data-source and generation-prompt documentation, and tempers categorical reasoning claims. These provide a limited gain in consistency and interpretation. The widespread score revisions lack an explanation establishing stronger validation, and removing the GPU count slightly reduces reproducibility detail.
